- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially > 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecasted drop magnitude.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward in next 5–10 days; cap forecast decline to 3–5% below peak.
- If sentiment turns positive late in history (e.g., last 3–5 days), model underreacts to upward momentum; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2% upward bias in final 5–7 days.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when recent prices are volatile; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast if 10–15 days of volatility precede forecast.
- When sentiment is neutral or weak (0.00–0.10 range), model tends to forecast flat or slightly downward; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for latent bullish sentiment.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply downward correction of 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If model forecast is <10% below true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply upward correction of 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days of true values show strong downward trend, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in final 5–7 days.
